doc.title: Sol Yaged interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 29, 2000

title: Sunday double header, hearing Goodman at 14 and his late wife
summary: Sol describes his Sunday gigs, hearing Benny Goodman on the radio in 1934 and buying a clarinet, and praises his wife and manager.

story.theme_name: Meeting, marrying and raising a family
story.community_name: Meeting, courting and marrying: musicians' love lives

blocks.x: I do a double header Tim, every Sunday. I play Sunday brunch at a place called Tony McGregor’s from 12-5, and then I go to a place called Danny’s Sea Palace from 7-11. I enjoy it. It doesn’t bother me.
That’s great. When you were 13 years old — I don’t know why I picked 13 — did you have aspirations to be a full time musician at that age?
Well when I heard Benny Goodman on the radio, I was about 13 years old then you’re right — what made you pick that year out?
Okay. I was born in 1922. If I was born in 1922, Monk, and I heard Benny Goodman on the radio in 1934, how old was I?

Okay then I was 14. I heard him do a radio broadcast with his band. And it was an unbelievable band. They were so hot I still get goose pimples talking about this band 60 years ago, 65 years ago. I says I’ve got to buy the clarinet. I didn’t know if I was going to be a professional or what. Thank God that’s all I’ve been doing all my life. I’ve been very fortunate. I wish my wife was here. I just lost my wife a few years ago. We were married for 51 glorious years. I’ll show you pictures of her later. She was my wife, my manager, my agent. And not for her I wouldn’t be here talking to you today my dear friend. She helped me every way and any way. She used to say to me Tim, my wife, “look, you play

the clarinet, I’ll take care of the business.” And she did. That’s why I’m living where I’m living now on 56th Street and Lexington Avenue for the past 25, 27 years. I’ll show you pictures of my wife later if you don’t mind, when she was 15 years old when I met her. 15. We got married my dear friend when she was 16, and we had our first child when my wife was 17 years old. Had I listened to her 30 years ago I would have been better off but I thought I knew all the answers. I thought I was going to be a star you know, stardom. A woman told me last night, she said to me last night Tim, are you listening to me, she says, “Sol, you’re the world’s greatest clarinet player.” I says, “How come?” She came up to me, she was crying, she says, “Mr. Yaged you’re the world’s greatest clarinet player.” I said, “how come?” She says, “Everybody else is dead.” And then she says, I belong in Hollywood.” She says, “The walk will do you good.” And you know what else she says to me, Monk? She says, “I belong on the stage.” She says, “It leaves in five minutes.”
